A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLOME research and contain 32 complete pages, including Appendices A.1–A.5. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable comparison of the scientific content and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Ehrlich sequence-optimization functions, including regret, feasibility, calibration, and sensitivity results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The LLOME optimization loops, MargE objective, reward function, dataset formatting, refinement, and filtering procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Ehrlich-function sequence-optimization tasks, including the same function-parameter and seed-dataset variations. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same genetic-algorithm comparator and SFT, DPO, MargE, and REINFORCE comparisons, including the multistage training variants.

E3.justification: The Pythia 2.8B model, oracle-evaluation budgets, one-epoch training rounds, evaluation metrics, and experimental settings in Section 5 and Appendices A.3–A.4 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical calibration, candidate-ranking, iterative-refinement, hyperparameter-sensitivity, multistage-training, and feasibility-versus-edit-distance analyses, including the appendix figures.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged: Figures 2 and 6 retain mean plus or minus two standard errors, while Figures 11 and 12 retain their stated 95% confidence intervals. No run-count or seed-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: The result figures and accompanying numerical and qualitative findings are identical. For example, both versions report that MargE reaches zero minimum regret by 24K function evaluations in Figure 2.

T1.justification: The Ehrlich-function definitions and constructions, MargE derivation, and Lemma 1 with its proof are unchanged, including Appendices A.1–A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning Ehrlich functions, LLOME, and MargE, together with the same claims about sample efficiency and optimization capabilities.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning DPO's feasibility problems, miscalibration, generator collapse, limited inference-time extrapolation, and the benefits of explicit rewards are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, input formatting, hyperparameter searches, optimizer settings, and training on two A100 GPUs remain unchanged in Appendices A.3–A.4. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Reference [16] identifies the same work in both versions; v3 merely adds its arXiv identifier and URL. No cited work is added or removed, and the research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates the arXiv version/date stamp and expands the bibliographic description of reference [16]. The main prose, terminology, section structure, and appendices are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded reference [16] occupies an additional line and slightly reflows the bibliography on page 14. Apart from the version stamp, all other rendered pages, including figures and algorithm displays, are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies an arXiv identifier and URL for an already identifiable reference and updates the version stamp. This modest bibliographic refinement leaves the scientific evidence, reasoning, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
